name: sccache
role: compiler cache wrapping nvcc for both setup.py's ninja compile and tools/ratify.py's post-build recompile, so the second compile of the same ten translation units is a cache hit instead of a repeat of the first
binary_sha256_recipe: sha256 over the raw bytes of the extracted `sccache` executable that is actually invoked (not the tarball) -- this is what tools/sccache_toolchain.py gates before use
why_this_target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl is a static binary (no glibc version coupling), matching the closed-world preference for a pin that behaves the same on any host, and it is the target sccache itself ships prebuilt (no cargo build needed).
why_not_gated_like_ptxas: sccache is a transparent pass-through wrapper: it execs the exact already-gated nvcc binary handed to it (tools/sccache_nvcc.py never resolves nvcc itself) and returns that nvcc's own output unmodified on a cache miss, or a byte-identical copy of a previous output on a cache hit -- measured, docs/build.md#sccache. Its version therefore cannot move ratified codegen the way a ptxas swap can, so a version drift is RECORDED (tools/ratify.py manifest toolchain.sccache) and REPORTED, not a hard ratchet failure. What IS gated hard, before the wrapper is used at all, is that the resolved `sccache` matches this pin -- an unpinned or tampered cache binary is REFUSED (Blake ruling 2026-08-28: 'a tool that can run one of two ways must REFUSE, not choose'). The only non-refusing outcome left is toolchain.sccache_enabled false in the dev config, an explicit, deliberate opt-out; the previous 'fall back to an uncached build and print a warning' default is gone -- a build no longer differs in whether it was cached by nothing more than which binaries happened to be on a host's PATH.
